title: The Letter of Port Mahon
premise: In 1746, the garrison town of Port Mahon runs on the rhythm of its observatory clock, tended by Rosalind Nakamura, a half-Japanese apprentice hiding behind her late father's trade name. When the army requisitions the town to build winter fortifications, they seize the harbor master's ledger — the only record proving which families hold legal residency — and Rosalind discovers her own name was never entered. As evictions begin and the river ice threatens to trap the displaced through a killing winter, she joins a smuggler's found family who forge passage papers for the condemned. The climax comes when Rosalind must decide which of two people she loves gets the single berth on the last ship before ice closes the river; she gives it away entirely, staying behind, and in the spring the town's freedmen and the clockmaker's guild force an inquiry that restores the stolen names — with hers written first.
about_author: Edmund Eastwick is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial port records before turning to fiction. He writes historical novels about the people history filed under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Escapement
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She climbs into the observatory tower to repair the master clock's escapement, establishing her precision, her hidden identity, and her habit of keeping busy hands over open words. Beat: quiet competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Redcoats post notices: the army takes the harbor quarter, and the residency ledger is confiscated as evidence of 'irregular settlement.' Her landlady burns letters in panic. Beat: the world's machinery begins grinding toward her.

chapters.title: The Missing Line
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She bribes a clerk to check the ledger copy and finds her name absent — her father registered his shop but never her. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve; she cannot appeal to a law that doesn't see her.

chapters.title: The Salt House
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Evicted families crowd the salt warehouse; among them old Tam Voss, a retired smuggler who once traded with her father. He offers shelter and asks no questions. Beat: first fragile thread of found family.

chapters.title: Names on Water
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. He remembers Rosalind's father forging bills of lading and recognizes the same careful hands in her. He shows her the network: fishermen, a defrocked priest, a widow who reads tides. Beat: warmth with an undertow of danger.

chapters.title: Paper Tide
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The crew forges their first passage papers using her engraving skills from clock-face work. A family slips out on a herring boat. Beat: purpose found — justice outside the law feels like winding a mechanism.

chapters.title: Lieutenant Hale
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The young requisition officer grows uneasy about the eviction quotas but obeys. He interviews shopkeepers and notes one clockmaker's apprentice who won't meet his eyes. Beat: antagonist as mirror — a man also trapped by paperwork.

chapters.title: The Widow's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Widow Serrano's POV. She calculates how many can leave before the river freezes: eleven berths, forty-three souls. Rosalind argues for taking everyone; Serrano teaches her the arithmetic of triage. Beat: idealism meeting cold necessity.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Soldiers search the salt house; Rosalind hides forged plates inside the observatory clock itself. Tam covers for her at cost of a beating. Beat: guilt — her cleverness endangered someone else.

chapters.title: Brother of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She finds Jun, a Japanese sailor stranded like she once was, working the docks. He calls her sister; he has no papers either. Beat: joy of kinship shadowed by the reader's knowledge that berths are finite.

chapters.title: Hale's Doubt
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Ordered to burn evicted families' belongings, Hale falsifies his first report instead. He begins quietly misfiling requisition orders. Beat: the system's own instrument beginning to bend.

chapters.title: The Ice Report
chapters.summary: Serrano's POV. Early frost upstream means the river will close in three weeks, not six. Panic rations hope. The crew must choose who sails first. Beat: dread made mathematical.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Jun's POV. Jun reveals he informed on a mutineer years ago to survive, and fears the army knows him. His presence endangers the whole network. Beat: the price of survival confessed aloud.

chapters.title: Betrayal's Shadow
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A raid nearly catches them; someone talked. Suspicion falls on Jun. Rosalind defends him against the crew's vote. Beat: loyalty tested against collective survival.

chapters.title: The Truth in the Tower
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She learns the informer was not Jun but the desperate clerk she bribed, broken under interrogation. She confesses her error to the crew. Beat: humility; her secret-keeping caused the wound.

chapters.title: Last Berth
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. One berth remains on the final ship. Both Jun and Tam — now dying of his beating injuries — need it. The chapter ends with Rosalind holding the ticket, unable to choose. Beat: the blurb's promise arriving.

chapters.title: What Rosalind Chose
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She gives the berth to neither decision alone: she puts Jun aboard with Tam's blessing, having forged a second paper she knew would fail inspection — sacrificing herself to draw the soldiers' attention at the dock. Beat: climax; love expressed as self-erasure.

chapters.title: Frozen River
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale watches Rosalind arrested, then does the unthinkable: he enters her name into the official ledger himself, making her legally real. Beat: justice attempted from inside the machine, too late and exactly in time.

chapters.title: The Clock Stops
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, from the cell. The master clock winds down unattended; the town loses its shared time. She repairs a guard's pocket watch, earning small mercies. Beat: endurance; identity sustained through craft.

chapters.title: Spring Inquiry
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The ice breaks; freed passengers testify. Serrano and the guild present the forged-but-truthful ledger pages. An inquiry voids the requisition's residency rulings. Beat: the tide turning through accumulated small acts.

chapters.title: Names Restored
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Released, she climbs the tower and restarts the master clock. In the new ledger, the guild clerk writes her full name — Nakamura and all — at the top. Jun returns upriver. Beat: restoration; time resumes.

chapters.title: The Letter of Port Mahon
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, years later. She receives a letter from a girl she once helped escape, now a clockmaker herself. Rosalind teaches apprentices in the salt house, where every window bears a name. Beat: found family enduring; survival's price paid forward.
